_comment: Path risk rules. Levels and triggers follow the original Shadow AI skill (High / Medium / Low / None). The numeric cut-offs marked proposal are Fluency proposals: the original text says only 'many hosts' and 'broad use'.

saas.high: any AI app with a content-read scope plus offline_access and no verified publisher (original rule)
saas.medium: user-consented AI apps that are not first-party, or an AI app from an unverified third-party publisher, or a Tier 1 service (original rule)
saas.low: only first-party, enterprise-tier or verified AI apps

endpoint.note: high: local model runners on 5 or more hosts (proposal); medium: 1 to 4 hosts, or non-first-party AI desktop apps on 10% or more of inventoried hosts (proposal); low: smaller desktop footprint; none: nothing found. First-party Microsoft Copilot is not counted.

detection.medium: no enabled EventWatch rule that is specific to AI use (original: 'no AI detection coverage' is Medium)

network.note: proposal: 1 or more unblocked uploads to AI services is Medium (original: broad use of consumer AI); 1,000 or more in the evidence window is High (proposal; the original says 'large uploads').

data.high: DLP matches coincide with AI use (original rule)
data.medium: DLP matches exist, one or no channel covered, or unblocked AI uploads
data.low: assessed, rating below Strong, nothing above
data.none: rating Strong and nothing found; not assessed when no DLP report evidence
